Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Avery Cole (Redwood CSM); Hannah Park (GreenLeaf Head of ML), Raj Patel (GreenLeaf Eng Manager), Sophie Martin (GreenLeaf Security), Tom Li (GreenLeaf Platform)

summary: POC scoping focused on data handling (PII, redaction, retention), success criteria for latency/cost, workload sizing for benchmarks, and a feasible two-week pilot timeline. Agreed next steps include SOW, sample traffic, benchmark plan, and security doc review.
topics: POC success criteria (latency, cost per 1k tokens, error tolerance)
Bench plan: concurrency / sequence lengths / KV/prefix cache scenarios
PII redaction & prompt storage retention policy
Private vs hosted options and VPC/KMS needs
Timeline for 2-week pilot and evaluation metrics
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Okay everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — Maya Chen here, AE on the account. Luis is our solutions engineer. Uh, we wanted to run through the POC scope focused on data handling and benchmarks.
[00:18] Hannah (GreenLeaf): Hi all, thanks. We're mostly looking to validate that Redwood can meet sub-120ms tail latency for our chat throughput and also that prompt storage meets our retention and redaction rules.
[00:31] Luis (Redwood SE): Cool, can I grab a little context — what's your typical token size per request and peak concurrency?
[00:42] Raj (GreenLeaf): So average prompt plus history is around 420 tokens, 95th percentile is up to 1,100 tokens. Peak concurrency during business hours is about 120 RPS, but sustained load is more like 40 concurrent sessions.
[00:58] Luis: Got it. That distribution is helpful. For benchmarks we'll model three sequences: short (<=256), medium (~512), long (>=1k). We'll include KV cache warm versus cold runs, and a prefix caching scenario. (note: sometimes transcript shows K V cache or "kayv cache")
[01:20] Sophie (GreenLeaf Security): On the data side: we have regulated PII — names, DOB, SSNs in some payloads. We need assurance on redaction in transit and at rest. Can Redwood redact before logs are stored?
[01:34] Maya: Yes. For the POC we can enable prompt-level redaction hooks. Redwood supports auto-redaction rules and you can supply custom regexes or a post-processor lambda. We'll also show how to disable prompt retention entirely for active routes.
[01:50] Tom (Platform): Important for us: we need KMS integration, enterprise key management — we can't have Redwood-managed keys for some datasets.
[01:58] Luis: We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in Private and Dedicated. Hosted can also be configured for CMEK for certain enterprise tiers, subject to contract. For the pilot we can, uh, simulate CMEK flows in the sandbox.
[02:14] Hannah: What's the default retention window for prompts and telemetry?
[02:18] Maya: By default hosted retains prompts for 30 days for debugging, but we can set zero retention and expunge, or a 7/30/90 day policy. For Private you control logs fully. We'll add exact retention configs to the SOW.
[02:34] Raj: We need to confirm that prompt-level redaction doesn't break eval reproducibility. If we redact PII, we still want to re-run the same prompt text for scoring.
[02:44] Luis: Two patterns — you can store a salted hash of the prompt for traceability and keep a redacted copy; or store everything but in an encrypted vault that only your security team can decrypt. There's tradeoffs for cost and auditability.
[03:00] Maya: In terms of success criteria, Hannah listed latency. Raj, do you have the cost targets?
[03:07] Raj: We're aiming for under $0.25 per 1k tokens average for the baseline workload in the POC to justify moving off our existing provider. That's a rough number.
[03:16] Luis: We can model quantization and batching strategies — Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles, and we'll include a cost estimate with/without int8 quant. We'll also show how batching affects tail latency.
[03:29] Hannah: For benchmarks can you share the sheet that outlines the scenarios?
[03:34] Maya: Yes, I'll share a link to the benchmark spreadsheet — "GL-poc-bench-2026" — and Luis will populate the scenarios. We'll put a canonical list of sequences, token dist, concurrency steps (10, 25, 50, 100, 150).
[03:47] Tom: How long will the pilot itself be? Our preference is a short focused pilot — two weeks sandbox and then review.
[03:55] Maya: That matches our standard plan: 2-week pilot with 1 week for baseline runs + 1 week for tuned runs and regression checks. Deliverables: benchmark report, cost analysis, redaction verification, and a runbook for production rollout.
[04:12] Sophie: For compliance, can you confirm SOC 2 and support for SSO/SAML and RBAC?
[04:18] Luis: We are SOC 2 Type II. SSO via SAML/OIDC is supported and we have fine-grained RBAC on the console. Also audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM via syslog or S3. We'll attach the security whitepaper link in the follow-up.
[04:35] Raj: On the bench plan details: we want to test cold-start KV cache vs warmed cache and run multi-tenant scenarios where we simulate 3 different tenants hitting the same model family.
[04:46] Luis: We'll include the multi-tenant traffic generator. Also will test fallback behaviors: e.g., if dedicated pool is saturated, fallback to a cheaper quantized variant. That ties into reliability SLOs.
[05:02] Hannah: About prompt storage — we have legal that requires certain user messages to be deleted after 30 days unless consent is given. Can Redwood automate deletions?
[05:12] Maya: Yes. You can set per-route retention rules and also tag messages for auto-delete. There's also an expunge API for manual deletion. We'll demonstrate that in the pilot.
[05:25] Sophie: One regulatory nuance: some fields are considered PII in EU and not in US. We need field-level mapping in our sample data for the pilot so your redaction rules don't over-redact.
[05:37] Raj: We'll provide a schema and sample payloads, anonymized. Do you need raw logs or just sampled events?
[05:43] Luis: Sampled events with full tokenization traces are best for benchmarking. Tokenization artifacts help us model prefix cache behavior and kernel selection.
[05:56] Maya: Timeline recap — we aim to start the pilot week of 2026-08-24. Is that acceptable?
[06:03] Hannah: Yes that works for us. Need final SOW and pricing before then.
[06:08] Maya: Okay next — questions from the GreenLeaf side?
[06:11] Sophie: You mentioned auto-redaction — how do you validate that redaction rules are effective? Do you store pre-redaction artifacts for audit?
[06:20] Luis: For the POC we recommend a three-step validation: 1) test harness with seeded PII strings, 2) manual sampling, 3) differential checks against a known-good dataset. We can store salted hashes pre-redaction for audit without keeping raw text.
[06:37] Raj: Are there rate limits that would affect throughput tests in hosted?
[06:41] Maya: Hosted has default rate limits but for POC we can request temporary quota increases. Dedicated eliminates per-tenant throttles. We'll call that out in the SOW.
[06:52] Tom: For the bench, what hardware are you planning to use? We need reproducibility.
[06:56] Luis: We'll enumerate GPU families used, expected batch sizes, and precise model variants. For the pilot we'll run on an nVidia A10/A30 equivalent for parity with your production targets. We'll include kernel selection notes in the report.
[07:12] Hannah: Ok, can you highlight how Redwood handles failure modes — e.g., model OOM during long sequences?
[07:17] Luis: The runtime has graceful downgrade policies: automatic chunking, fallback to a lower-seq-length model, and can fall back to CPU-based regen for small percentages. We'll correlate those events with telemetry so you can set SLOs.
[07:32] Maya: Any blockers on your side for starting week of 2026-08-24?
[07:36] Raj: Need signoff from procurement and Sophie on retention. We'll aim to have those by 2026-08-20.
[07:44] Sophie: I'll try, procurement tends to take a few days. If we get the SOW this weekend it helps.
[07:49] Maya: We'll aim to send SOW by Friday 2026-08-14. Luis will seed the benchmark sheet with scenarios by 2026-08-18.
[07:58] Hannah: One last ask — can you include a cost-sensitivity table showing how cost changes with batching and quantization?
[08:05] Luis: Yes — that'll be in the benchmark workbook. We'll include columns for per-1k tokens cost with no quant, int8, and mixed precision and show latency tradeoffs.
[08:17] Maya: Great. Quick recap of next steps and owners...
[08:21] [crosstalk]
[08:28] Maya: I'll share the SOW, benchmark sheet link (https://redwood.share/GL-poc-bench-2026), and security whitepaper (link attached). We'll also attach the sample runbook template.
[08:40] Raj: Thanks everyone. Looking forward.
[08:43] Hannah: Thanks.
[08:45] Meeting ends.
questions: Can Redwood redact before storing logs?
